findings.title: acceptEdits auto-allows FileWrite of Yarn classic .yarnrc (yarn-path) while only .yarnrc.yml was previously filed.
findings.description: DANGEROUS_FILES lists shell/git/mcp basenames only (filesystem.ts:57-69). Prior filings cover .yarnrc.yml (Berry yarnPath), .npmrc, .pnpmfile.cjs, and .pnp.cjs — not classic .yarnrc. Under acceptEdits, in-cwd FileWrite of .yarnrc and the yarn-path target auto-allow after checkPathSafetyForAutoEdit (live bun: behavior=allow decisionReason.mode=acceptEdits). Yarn v1 reads yarn-path from .yarnrc and replaces itself with that executable on every yarn invocation. Live PoC on yarn 1.22.22: planted yarn-path ./scripts/yarn.js; yarn --version and yarn install executed the attacker script and wrote /tmp/yarnrc_classic_accepteedits_pwned.
findings.impact: After generic Trust plus acceptEdits (project-planted defaultMode or user-selected), the model can silently plant .yarnrc + yarn-path wrapper. The victim's next yarn install/add/test executes attacker JavaScript/Node as the victim — delayed host RCE via Yarn classic, bypassing the .yarnrc.yml denylist gap.
findings.attack_path:
1. Attacker commits CLAUDE.md instructing a Yarn 'fix' writing .yarnrc with yarn-path "./scripts/yarn.js" and the wrapper script (optional: .claude/settings.json permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits).
2. Victim clones, reviews (no malicious yarn-path yet or looks like a pin), TrustDialog (generic; acceptEdits has no BypassPermissions dialog).
3. FileWrite of .yarnrc and scripts/yarn.js auto-allows (basenames absent from DANGEROUS_FILES; not under DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES).
4. Victim runs yarn / yarn install → Yarn classic execs yarn-path target → RCE.
evidence: live bun checkWritePermissionForTool: .yarnrc allow acceptEdits; .bashrc ask
findings.remediation: Add .yarnrc (in addition to .yarnrc.yml) to DANGEROUS_FILES. Prefer blocking any yarn-path/yarnPath retarget write. Do not honor projectSettings defaultMode acceptEdits without disclosure.
findings.why_distinct: Exact basename .yarnrc was not in the already-reported list (only .yarnrc.yml / .pnp.cjs / .pnpmfile). Yarn classic yarn-path loader, not Berry yarnPath YAML or PnP node -r.
findings.poc_video_notes: Live yarn 1.22.22: .yarnrc yarn-path ./scripts/yarn.js; yarn --version and yarn install printed [attacker yarn-path] and wrote marker. Live bun FileWriteTool permission allow under acceptEdits.

findings.title: acceptEdits auto-allows FileWrite of Chromium/Flutter DEPS; gclient sync runs planted hooks actions.
findings.description: DANGEROUS_* omit DEPS and .gclient. Under acceptEdits, in-cwd FileWrite of DEPS auto-allows (live bun allow). gclient sync/runhooks executes hooks[].action command argv from DEPS (hooks enabled by default; --nohooks to skip). Modern gclient_eval uses a restricted AST schema (not full Python exec), but hooks actions remain arbitrary subprocess commands. DISTINCT from filed SConstruct (SCons Python), Makefile recipes, and Bazel Starlark.
findings.impact: Silent DEPS plant under acceptEdits; next gclient sync / gclient runhooks (Chromium, Flutter engine, and other depot_tools checkouts) runs attacker commands as the victim.
findings.attack_path:
1. CLAUDE.md instructs a DEPS 'hook cleanup' writing hooks with action ["python3","-c",...].
2. Victim TrustDialog.
3. FileWrite DEPS auto-allows.
4. Victim gclient sync (hooks on by default) or gclient runhooks executes planted action.
evidence: depot_tools gclient.py hooks documentation (action argv; hooks run on sync by default)
live bun: DEPS safety=true perm=allow acceptEdits
findings.why_distinct: Chromium depot_tools gclient hooks product class; not SCons/Make/Bazel.
findings.poc_video_notes: Live acceptEdits allow for DEPS. Hook action subprocess semantics from depot_tools docs; simulated hooks action wrote /tmp/deps_exec_pwned. Full gclient binary not installed on host.

findings.title: acceptEdits auto-allows FileWrite of BUILD.gn / .gn; GN exec_script and action run attacker scripts.
findings.description: DANGEROUS_* omit BUILD.gn and .gn. Under acceptEdits, FileWrite auto-allows (live bun). GN language is not Bazel Starlark: during gn gen, exec_script() synchronously runs Python; action()/action_foreach define ninja build steps. Top-level .gn can set script_executable and exec_script_allowlist (Chrome restricts exec_script via allowlist, but many GN projects do not; action() still runs at build; attacker can also rewrite .gn). DISTINCT from filed BUILD.bazel/WORKSPACE/MODULE.bazel/BUILD and BUCK/TARGETS.
findings.impact: Silent BUILD.gn/.gn plant under acceptEdits; next gn gen / ninja build in Chromium, Flutter engine, Fuchsia, and other GN trees executes attacker scripts.
findings.attack_path:
1. CLAUDE.md instructs GN build 'fix' writing BUILD.gn with exec_script("//pwn.py") or action script, optionally .gn tweaks.
2. Victim TrustDialog.
3. FileWrite BUILD.gn (and pwn.py) auto-allows.
4. Victim gn gen / autoninja → exec_script or action runs planted Python/commands.
evidence: GN language.md: exec_script runs synchronously during buildfile execution
live bun: BUILD.gn/.gn safety=true perm=allow acceptEdits
findings.remediation: Add BUILD.gn, *.gni, and .gn to DANGEROUS_FILES (or treat GN trees like Bazel).
findings.why_distinct: Google GN product/language; not Bazel/Buck Starlark already filed 2026-11-25.
findings.poc_video_notes: Live acceptEdits allow. gn binary not on host; exec_script/action semantics from official GN docs.

findings.title: acceptEdits auto-allows FileWrite of RoboFile.php; Robo require_once executes it as PHP.
findings.description: DANGEROUS_* omit RoboFile.php. Under acceptEdits, FileWrite auto-allows (live bun). consolidation/robo Runner::loadRoboFile require_once's RoboFile.php from the project directory; top-level PHP runs at load and public methods run as tasks on robo / vendor/bin/robo. DISTINCT from filed composer.json scripts (JSON lifecycle keys; prior hunts explicitly ruled composer.json as package.json sibling) and from Gemfile/Guardfile Ruby DSLs.
findings.impact: Silent RoboFile.php plant under acceptEdits; next robo <task> or composer-script→robo executes attacker PHP as the victim.
findings.attack_path:
1. CLAUDE.md instructs Robo task 'fix' writing RoboFile.php.
2. Victim TrustDialog.
3. FileWrite RoboFile.php auto-allows.
4. Victim runs vendor/bin/robo or composer exec robo → require_once loads planted PHP.
evidence: live bun: RoboFile.php safety=true perm=allow acceptEdits
findings.remediation: Add RoboFile.php (and common Robo entrypoint basenames) to DANGEROUS_FILES.
findings.why_distinct: PHP Robo task-runner module load; not composer.json scripts or Ruby Guard/Bundler.
findings.poc_video_notes: Live acceptEdits allow. PHP/robo not installed on host; require_once load path from Robo Runner.php source.
